content_metadata.description: The video features Parisa Najafi, a professor, explaining the concept of planar packing factor for the 111 plane in a Body-Centered Cubic (BCC) structure.

qAndA.answer: The center atom plays a key role in determining the geometry of the 111 plane, influencing the calculations for the base and height of the triangle that represents it.
qAndA.question: Why is the center atom in the BCC structure important for calculating the planar packing factor?

qAndA.answer: Only atoms whose center lies on the plane itself are considered when calculating planar density. The center atom of the BCC structure does not lie on the 111 plane, hence it's excluded.
qAndA.question: Why doesn't the center atom in the 111 plane contribute to the planar density?

qAndA.answer: The planar packing factor is calculated as the area of the atoms on the plane divided by the area of the plane.
